title: Port and dry reds
subtitle: Two wines, one grape
objectives: Explain Touriga Nacional's role in Port

steps.title: In Port
steps.body: Port is a blend of many grapes. Touriga Nacional brings colour, tannin, structure and its floral perfume, essential for Vintage Port, which must age for decades. It is usually a smaller share than Touriga Franca, the Douro's most planted grape, because of its lower yields. Most Port grapes are foot-trodden or machine-trodden in lagares.

steps.title: Dry reds
steps.body: Since the 1990s, the Douro has become famous for dry reds, often blends of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca and Tinta Roriz. Barca Velha, first made in 1952, showed the potential. Today single-varietal Touriga Nacional from the Douro and Dão is common, often aged in French oak.

steps.prompt: What does Touriga Nacional bring to Port?
steps.explanation: Touriga Nacional is aromatic, not neutral.

steps.body: Try a Douro dry red and a ruby Port side by side. The violet and dark fruit of Touriga Nacional link both, though one is dry and the other sweet.

steps.prompt: Barca Velha, an early Douro dry red, was first made in ____.
steps.explanation: 1952. It showed that the Douro could make great dry reds.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Touriga Nacional gives Port colour, structure and perfume
The Douro now makes famous dry reds, since Barca Velha in 1952
Dry and sweet styles share its violet and dark fruit
